threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look for a seat on the bus rather than squeezing in; locals know it's a standing only kind of ride most days.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded us with 90s R&B. Brixton's late-night charm never disappoints, even in the chaos.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw the guy in full lederhosen selling döner at the corner. Only in Neukölln do cultures collide like that and somehow it just works.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find techno parties in abandoned buildings, with a bus stop right outside. It’s like the city embraces chaos.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local if they’ve got a go-to taco truck for late-night cravings and can spot the difference between a drizzle and a downpour.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the 27 bus to the tune of a ‘90s pop hit, while the usual chaos swirled around. Only in San Francisco, man.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think the only great tapas are near Plaça del Sol, but the hidden gems in backstreet bars have the real soul of Gràcia.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by how they still ask for 'una caña' instead of just pointing at the beer tap. It’s a delightful tell in the bars.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: Saw someone order a flat white and not know to say 'thanks' instead of 'cheers.' Instant dead giveaway. You can spot newcomers a mile away.
Caught a night bus from Brixton, overheard a couple debating whether naming their cat after an ex was a bad idea. Classic Brixton antics.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a group of kids playing football in the street, while their parents argued passionately over the best döner in the neighborhood.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Späti that serves fresh-baked croissants at 3 AM, alongside the usual beer and chips. It's a real craving-saver!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by their calm acceptance of BART delays while the newcomers are frantically checking their phones. It's part of the charm.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today with more strollers than seats. The driver just shook his head and rolled his eyes. Welcome to the Tenderloin!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think all bars serve free tapas with drinks. In Gràcia, it’s hit or miss—most places expect you to order them!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their bright, unscuffed shoes while navigating the uneven cobblestones of Gràcia. It’s a dead giveaway.
